solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Don tries cutting material in final run-through

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on, i.e. to dress

indicators.note: the trial word slices into the word for material, sitting inside it

parts.note: material in the sense of physical, substantial: real
a judge tries a case, i.e. hears it

explanation.surface: A man named Don makes attempts at trimming fabric before the last rehearsal of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a name but is the verb 'put on'; 'material' is the adjective (real), not cloth. HEARS cutting REAL gives REHEARSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The full rehearsal in costume just before opening night is the final complete practice performance.

clue.text: Turned up in badly made trousers, sweetheart?

indicators.note: something badly made is put together wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A query whether a lover is found inside poorly tailored trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet', its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A retroussé nose is one tipped upward at the end, so the French borrowing means upturned.

clue.text: Formula 1 racing circuit in the country

parts.note: Spa-Francorchamps in Belgium hosts the Belgian Grand Prix, usually just called Spa

explanation.surface: A Grand Prix track located somewhere in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside but names a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation of the Iberian peninsula, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Give up and eat up dire stew

indicators.note: to stew things is to mix them in a pot, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Instructions to abandon a diet and finish an awful casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate something is to renounce or disown it, which is to abandon it.

clue.text: Covert clothing for gangsters

definitions.meaning: garments that cover and conceal the head and face

explanation.definitionFit: A hood is head-covering clothing, and in American slang hoods are hoodlums, i.e. criminals.

clue.text: Goalies off to catch Jerry? Excuses to be made!

indicators.note: the scrambled keepers enclose the chamber pot, as if catching it
off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: jerry is British slang for a chamber pot, a PO

explanation.surface: Football keepers fail to hold a German, and need excuses for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry' seems to be a German or a name; it is British slang for a chamber pot, PO. 'off' signals the anagram of GOALIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apologies offered for a failure are justifications or pleas of regret, much like excuses.

clue.text: Son has desire for animal food

parts.note: will means wish or desire

explanation.surface: A boy wants something for feeding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is kitchen waste mixed with liquid and fed to pigs, so it is livestock feed.

clue.text: Nutter left girl with muscular spasm

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

explanation.surface: A madman abandoned a young woman who has a twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as abandoned but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutter is British slang for a crazy person, a madman.

clue.text: MP (left-winger) gets better

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: A socialist Member of Parliament improves.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like Member of Parliament but means military policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: British military police are nicknamed for the red covers on their caps, so the nickname means a military policeman.

clue.text: Spear-carrier turning right in fire

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembly is read backwards
the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for fire

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them, i.e. to axe

explanation.surface: A soldier with a spear veers right while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses ARTXE (RT in AXE) as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear-carrier is a walk-on actor with no lines, a theatrical bit player in a crowd scene.

clue.text: Pushing for progress

definitions.meaning: pushing a product means publicising or advertising it
advancement in rank or position at work

explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is both the marketing of goods and advancement to a higher job.

clue.text: Councillor kept sovereign

parts.note: kept in the sense of possessed: owned

explanation.surface: A local councillor held on to a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the coin but is the adjective, ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A head that has been invested with royal regalia rules as monarch, so crowned means reigning.

clue.text: Drug seen in fissure is made the centre of attention

indicators.note: the drug is found inside the crack

parts.note: a slit is a narrow crack
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Cannabis spotted in a crack becomes the focus of everyone's interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lit by a stage beam is picked out for everyone to look at, so it is the focus of interest.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian gum

parts.note: ancient means long ago, past
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as in E£ for the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: A resin from the time of the pharaohs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Egyptian' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a sticky adhesive, and to gum things is to glue them, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Former employer initially axed worker for performing

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: axed means cut
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: An ex-boss first sacked a staff member for doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An executant is one who carries out or performs something, especially music, so as an adjective it means doing or performing.

clue.text: Ungodly fellow is in garret

indicators.note: the man and is sit inside the loft

parts.note: a garret is an attic room
he stands for a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A wicked man lives up in the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies the existence of any deity has a godless outlook, so the adjective means ungodly.

clue.text: Successfully defend river and speak at length

parts.note: to hold a position is to defend it successfully
the Forth is a Scottish river flowing to Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Keep a position by the water and make a long speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successfully defend river' suggests holding the fort, but the fort is part of the river name, Scotland's Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth is an idiom for talking lengthily and pompously on a subject.

clue.text: Can first one in get kitchen utensil?

parts.note: a can is a tin
an opener is the first to go in, e.g. an opening batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A question whether going in first lets one obtain a cooking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb 'is able to' but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for cutting the lids off cans is a standard piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Story spread in stages

parts.note: a piece is a newspaper article or story
a spread is a lavish meal

explanation.surface: A tale told gradually, bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done a bit at a time, gradually, is the meaning of the adverb, as with work done in instalments.

clue.text: Fondle girl on one's knee

indicators.note: in a down entry the girl's name sits on top of, i.e. after, the fondling word

parts.note: to pat is to caress lightly
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Stroke a young woman sitting on your lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one's knee' reads as one phrase about a lap, but 'on' is a placement word in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap bone is the anatomical name for the bone at the front of the leg joint.

clue.text: Fellows hold Yankee back in council

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled word is read in reverse
the college fellows hold the letter inside them

parts.note: dons are university fellows
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: College fellows keep an American back at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DONYS, made by Y held in DONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy, a kind of ecclesiastical council.

clue.text: Abhor English international supporting Germany

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting pieces lie beneath the country's letter

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A sports fan hates an England fixture backing the Germans.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a direct synonym of abhor.

clue.text: In the US cuffs provide surprises

definitions.meaning: what Americans call cuffs, the folded-up hems of trouser legs, are the British term

explanation.definitionFit: British trouser hems folded back are called by the phrase, which also means an unexpected development.

clue.text: Managed Chinese farm

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone ran an agricultural business in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Protest is over money

indicators.note: over signals that the word is is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A demonstration is about pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about' but reverses IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a place in protest is a form of demonstration where participants refuse to move.

clue.text: Feet no good? Mark's a worrier!

parts.note: f is an abbreviation for foot or feet
US stands for unserviceable, i.e. useless or no good
a spot is a mark or stain

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about bad feet and a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone who frets over trifles, a person who worries excessively.

clue.text: Scrap bit of roofing kept in outhouse

indicators.note: the letter is stored inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its first letter here

explanation.surface: Waste pieces of roofing material stored in an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small torn piece, a scrap or fragment.

clue.text: Ancestral building — a royal house

indicators.note: building means assembling, so these letters are constructed anew

explanation.surface: A family seat is the home of a monarch's dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun (the ancestral home) but is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English dynasty in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Queen finishes in tears

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: A queen ends up crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests weeping but is the verb, rips.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to rip apart, so rends means rips, the verb sense of tears.

clue.text: Wild stab made by night-time assassin

definitions.meaning: a gunshot fired by a killer under cover of darkness

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a guess made with no real knowledge, and literally a gunfire blast in blackness.
